The bound-removed build IS caught, but by a different case: 'must-still-collapse beyond-sanity-bound' (smoke.ts:337-341, MUST_COLLAPSE lane), which is the evidence cited for the separate intent CHK-001:edge:1, not for edge:0. So CHK-001:edge:0 has no valid evidence of its own claimed property; that property is established elsewhere under a different intentRef. This is an evidence note that restates the intent rather than an assertion that proves it. Net risk is low (the bound is genuinely tested by edge:1), but the edge:0 evidence record itself does not cover what it claims.
findings.resolvedReason: Replaced the tautological sanity-bound assertion. MAX_REASON_CHARS is now exported from convergence-breaker.ts and the smoke asserts gateFailureDigest(cmd, TRANSCRIPT) === gateFailureDigest(cmd, TRANSCRIPT.slice(0, MAX_REASON_CHARS)) as matrix case 'sanity-bound-is-applied'. Revert-proof against the built dist: deleting .slice(0, MAX_REASON_CHARS) fails exactly sanity-bound/sanity-bound-is-applied and sanity-bound/beyond-sanity-bound, 18 other cases still passing — the old well-formed-digest check passed under that same deletion. findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/convergence-breaker.ts:510 — the narrowed digit-rule regex `(?<![\w-])\d+(?![\w-])` only treats a digit run as identifier-attached when preceded/followed by a word char or ASCII hyphen; a `.` does not protect. Verified empirically: normalize("requires lattice-cli v0.3.229 or newer") and normalize("requires lattice-cli v0.3.230 or newer") both reduce to "requires lattice-cli v0.#.# or newer" (identical digest). Any rejection reason embedding a dotted version/semver string (a realistic shape given version-bump.ts already formats messages like "expected X.Y.Z") collapses two substantively different failures into one gate-failure key -- exactly the C4 over-collapse class this story exists to fix, for a token shape CHK-003/CHK-004 never exercises. gateFailureDigest is exported general-purpose, not scoped to the one current call site.
findings.resolvedReason: The number rule's protection set was widened from [\w-] to [\w.-], so a digit run attached by a dot is treated as part of the identifier: 'requires lattice-cli v0.3.229 or newer' and the same message with v0.3.230 now keep separate digest keys. Guarded by must-differ case 'dotted-version-requirement' (guard: digit-rule), which drives the real counter and asserts keys=2 counter=1. Revert-proof: restoring the round-1 form (?<![\w-])\d+(?![\w-]) fails digit-rule/dotted-version-requirement and digit-rule/negative-counter with the other 18 passing.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/convergence-breaker.ts:510 — the digit-rule lookbehind/lookahead `(?<![\w-])...(?![\w-])` excludes a preceding/following ASCII hyphen unconditionally, which also matches a minus sign, so a negative number is treated as identifier-attached and survives instead of collapsing. Verified: normalize("retry budget -5 remaining") vs normalize("retry budget -19 remaining") do NOT collapse (stay distinct), unlike the documented free-standing-counter behavior in the surrounding comment (attempt 41, 3>=2, 0/4 lanes all correctly collapse). This under-collapses an incidental numeric difference, i.e. it is a live instance of the exact risk plan.md #4 calls out as the change's central danger ("the change makes the breaker fire less often ... a stuck agent [could] regain an unbounded retry loop"), for a token shape (negative numbers) the CHK-004 must-still-collapse lane never tests.
findings.resolvedReason: Re-decided in round 4 and recorded as superseded rather than silently reverted. This finding asked the digest to collapse -5 and -19 by treating a leading minus as a sign rather than an identifier hyphen. Honouring it requires the general free-standing-number rule, and that rule is exactly what collapsed the F-020 shapes — it cannot distinguish retry budget -5 from got -0.61 in real test output. No producer in this tree emits a bare countdown into a gate rejection, so the finding asked the digest to collapse an ambiguous bare number with nothing on the volatile side of the scale. The fixture is NOT deleted: it is converted to must-differ case negative-counter-now-distinct, tagged number-rule-removal, so the change of decision is visible in the matrix output. Rationale and residual recorded in plan.md section 4.2 and 4.3.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/convergence-breaker.ts:463-468 — the function's top JSDoc still states the error message is "normalized to strip volatile tokens (hashes, ids, timestamps, bare numbers, paths)" unqualified. This is now inaccurate: CHK-002 narrowed path-stripping to token-start absolute paths only (relative repo paths and mid-token slashes like DEV/REVIEW are deliberately left untouched), and CHK-003 narrowed number-stripping to standalone numbers only (identifier-attached digits like CHK-001 are deliberately preserved). A maintainer reading only this doc comment would believe ALL paths and ALL bare numbers are still stripped, which is precisely the kind of doc/implementation mismatch this story's own root cause (an over-broad implementation vs. a narrower intended contract) illustrates. The doc comment should name the narrower rule (token-start absolute paths; standalone digit runs) so a future edit does not re-widen the regex believing it is restoring documented behavior.
findings.resolvedReason: The gateFailureDigest JSDoc was rewritten from the unqualified 'bare numbers, paths' claim to a per-rule description of what the normalizer actually does: hex/0x/ISO tokens; absolute paths ONLY at a token start (POSIX and Windows) with relative repo paths and mid-token slashes explicitly named as deliberately untouched; durations/sizes with a unit suffix; and standalone numbers only, with identifier-attached digits (CHK-001, B-bf52, round-2, v0.3.229) explicitly named as deliberately preserved. It also states that widening re-introduces the false freeze and that narrowing the duration/number rule re-introduces the livelock, and points at the smoke as the case-by-case guard. The retained sanity bound got its own exported doc comment.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/convergence-breaker.ts:502 — the path-rule regex `(?:^|(?<=[\s"'(\[]))\/[^\s"')\]]*` only recognizes POSIX-style absolute paths (leading `/`). A Windows-style absolute path such as `C:\Users\jek\file1.ts` vs `C:\Users\other\file2.ts` is left completely untouched by every normalization rule (no leading slash, and digits inside `file1`/`file2` are word-attached so the digit-rule also leaves them alone) and so the two machine-specific paths do NOT collapse to one digest -- verified empirically. The design comment at :500-501 explicitly claims the rule "behaves identically on macOS and Linux" (i.e. Windows was consciously out of scope), so this may be an accepted gap rather than an oversight, but it reproduces the same host-varying-path-does-not-collapse failure mode this story exists to fix if this CLI is ever run from a Windows host.
findings.resolvedReason: Windows absolute paths are now normalized by a dedicated rule (?:^|(?<=[\s"'(\[:=,]))[a-z]:\\[^\s"')\]]* applied before the POSIX rule, and the token-start delimiter set of both path rules was widened to include : = and , so a path introduced without a separating space (cwd=/Users/...) also collapses. Guarded by must-still-collapse cases 'windows-absolute-path' (guard: windows-path-rule) and 'delimiter-attached-absolute-path' (guard: path-rule). Revert-proof: deleting the Windows rule fails exactly windows-path-rule/windows-absolute-path with the other 19 passing.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/convergence-breaker.ts:510 the narrowed standalone-number rule `(?<![\w-])\d+(?![\w-])` does not normalize a digit run directly attached to a UNIT-LETTER suffix (e.g. 45s, 5m, 2h) because the follow-char is a word character, so the negative lookahead blocks the match. Three real, story_advance-reachable rejection messages embed exactly this shape via formatLeaseAge/formatLockAge (heartbeat `${age} ago`, age like 45s/5m/2h): (1) packages/main/src/core/story-owner-lease.ts:591-598,616-640 formatLeaseAge/formatNonOwnerError (thrown from cli/ownership-gate.ts non-owner story_advance rejection -- the common no-lease-owned-by-me path), (2) packages/main/src/cli/ownership-gate.ts:301-306 active-lease --takeover rejection, (3) packages/main/src/core/main-write-lock.ts:71-113 formatLockAge/buildMainWriteLockContentionMessage (DONE-phase main-write-lock contention), (4) packages/main/src/core/validation-execution-lock.ts:233-262 formatLockAge/buildValidationLockContentionMessage (TEST-phase validation-lock contention). Verified against the built packages/main/dist/core/convergence-breaker.js: gateFailureDigest(story_advance, msg-with-45s) !== gateFailureDigest(story_advance, msg-with-46s) for all four message shapes (confirmed by direct node execution), so a story_advance retried against an actively-heartbeating foreign lease or a held lock gets a NEW digest key on essentially every retry and maxGateFailureCount never reaches 2 -- assessBreaker never trips gate-repeat for exactly the runaway-retry-loop scenario the breaker exists to catch. Confirmed this is a functional REGRESSION: the OLD unconditional /\d+/g rule DID collapse these same two messages to one key (verified directly), so narrowing broke a previously-working case. This also falsifies the CHK-003 verificationIntent edge claim recorded in plan.md #3 (Confirmed no production rejection message embeds a volatile counter attached to an identifier: the only attached-counter shapes in the tree are step record ids at planned-steps-executor.ts:1298 and :1309, and that module throws no Error) -- that module indeed throws nothing, but the heartbeat-age shape above DOES throw reachable Errors and was missed by that survey. None of CHK-004s must-still-collapse matrix cases (packages/main/src/tasks/convergence-breaker-smoke.ts) exercise a digit-attached-to-unit-letter shape -- its only counter/timestamp case uses ISO-8601 timestamps plus a free-standing (attempt N) counter -- so the regression guard does not catch this. Fix: normalize the digit+unit-letter age shape (e.g. \\b\\d+[smh]\\b) before/alongside the standalone-number rule, or normalize via the formatted age helper output generally.
findings.resolvedReason: Confirmed as a functional regression and fixed with a duration/size rule (?<![\w.-])-?\d+(?:\.\d+)?(?:ms|s|m|h|d|kb|mb|gb|b)(?![\w.-]) applied immediately before the number rule, so a digit run welded to a unit letter is consumed together with its unit. All four story_advance-reachable sources named in the finding are now must-still-collapse fixtures reproduced from their build sites — story-owner-lease.ts:616-640 (formatNonOwnerError), cli/ownership-gate.ts:301-306 (active-lease --takeover refusal), main-write-lock.ts:96-118 and validation-execution-lock.ts:243-262 — each varying only the heartbeat age (and the holder pid where present), each asserting keys=1 counter=2 and that assessBreaker trips with gate-repeat 2>=2. Revert-proof: deleting the duration rule fails exactly those four cases (duration-rule/lease-non-owner-heartbeat-age, active-lease-takeover-refusal, main-write-lock-contention, validation-lock-contention) and leaves the other 16 passing. plan.md section 3 was rewritten to retract the false survey claim this finding disproved, name the four sources and record the duration rule as the answer.

Suggest tightening CHK-001/002/003 userSees to describe the actual tag+keys/counter/breaker format rather than implying literal value names are printed.
findings.resolvedReason: userSees is frozen, so the OUTPUT was changed to match the promise instead. Every matrix case now prints its two literal compared reason values under its tag, plus the verdict in words ('the two values DIGEST DIFFERENTLY' / 'DIGEST IDENTICALLY') and the index of the first character at which the pair diverges. DEV/REVIEW vs DEV/TEST, /Users vs /private/var, CHK-001 vs CHK-002 and src/core/alpha.ts vs src/core/beta.ts now appear literally on screen. Values longer than 150 chars print a window centred on the first differing character rather than a head-truncated prefix, because the DEV-gate pair is byte-identical for its first 617 characters — a head preview would have printed two identical strings and shown nothing, and the printed divergence index is itself the CHK-001 evidence that the difference lies past the former 200-character cut.

findings.desc: cross-host (codex-cli host-B) finding, recorded by the main agent because codex-cli is not a registered dispatch actor: packages/main/src/core/convergence-breaker.ts — MAX_REASON_CHARS slices the RAW reason as UTF-16 code units before normalization, so a reason of the form 'x'.repeat(16383) + an astral character leaves a lone high surrogate (0xd83d) as the final unit, which hashes as replacement encoding rather than the original character. Deterministic, so no cross-call instability, but the bound is not Unicode code-point safe. Fix: drop a trailing lone high surrogate after the slice.
findings.resolvedReason: The sanity bound is now applied by boundReasonForDigest(), which slices to MAX_REASON_CHARS and then drops a trailing lone high surrogate (charCode in 0xd800-0xdbff), so the bound can no longer leave half of an astral character to be hashed as a replacement encoding. Evidence strength recorded as medium: the surrogate trim itself is covered by inspection and the direction check rather than by a dedicated smoke fixture, since the observable consequence is a digest-input difference and not a behavioural divergence. The same finding's path-delimiter half is fixed and guarded as described under F-006.

packages/main/src/core/convergence-breaker.ts:538 the pre-existing hex-id rule /\b[0-9a-f]{7,}\b/g runs BEFORE the CHK-003 number rule (:581) and has no identifier-attachment protection (only a bare \b word-boundary, not the [\w.-] lookbehind/lookahead the number rule uses). Since decimal digits 0-9 are a subset of hex digits 0-9a-f, ANY identifier-attached decimal digit run of 7+ characters is consumed by this earlier rule before the number rule ever sees it, so CHK-003s documented contract (checklist.json CHK-003:edge:1: a story id whose digits are attached to an identifier survives normalization; JSDoc :523-526) silently fails once the digit run reaches 7 characters. Verified against the built module: gateFailureDigest(cmd,gate BLOCKED: session-1234567 failed) === gateFailureDigest(cmd,gate BLOCKED: session-7654321 failed) COLLAPSE, and worker-1721775600 vs worker-1721775601 (epoch-suffixed ids) also COLLAPSE -- while the identical construction with a 6-digit suffix (session-123456 vs session-654321) correctly stays DISTINCT, proving the 7-digit hex-rule threshold is exactly what breaks the promise. This is an over-collapse: two DIFFERENT identifiers (e.g. two different epoch-timestamp-suffixed session/worker ids, or any numeric identifier reaching 7 digits) read as one gate failing twice -- precisely the false-freeze failure mode this story exists to eliminate -- and it is not covered by any MUST_DIFFER matrix case (checklist-ordinal/review-round-ordinal/story-id/dotted-version-requirement all use digit runs under 7 characters, so the matrix never exercises this rule-ordering interaction).

packages/main/src/core/convergence-breaker.ts:568 and :581 -- the widened [\w.-] protection set added by this round (F-002/F-007) makes the duration rules and the number rules trailing lookahead (?![\w.-]) treat a literal sentence-ending period (no preceding space) as a protected identifier character, so a standalone counter or duration immediately followed by . fails to normalize. Verified against the built module: gateFailureDigest(cmd,Retry count exceeded 5.) !== gateFailureDigest(cmd,Retry count exceeded 19.) (DISTINCT -- should collapse, both are free-standing counters differing only in incidental value) and the same holds for the duration rule (heartbeat 45s. vs heartbeat 46s. stay DISTINCT while heartbeat 45s  vs heartbeat 46s  with a trailing space correctly COLLAPSE). It reintroduces the same under-collapse class that F-007 fixed for units (a livelock that never accumulates because every retry mints a fresh key), for any rejection message that happens to end a bare number/duration right before a period with no separating space -- a common English sentence-final construction. Not covered by the smoke matrix: the closest fixture (negative-counter, MUST_COLLAPSE) uses -5 remaining before the gate refuses (trailing space), never a trailing period.

The fixture is converted to must-differ case sentence-final-counter-now-distinct rather than deleted, so the re-decision is visible in the matrix. findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/convergence-breaker.ts:556 vs :588/:612 — the round-3 F-014 fix gave the hex rule identifier-attachment lookarounds (?<![\w-])...(?![\w-]) but NOT the dot-adjacency lookarounds (?<!\d\.)/(?!\.\d) that the round-3 F-015 fix gave the duration rule (:588) and number rule (:612). Since the hex rule runs first and decimal digits are a subset of hex digits, a FREE-STANDING (non-identifier-attached) decimal number or duration whose integer part is >=7 digits gets its integer part eaten by the hex rule alone, before the duration/number rule ever sees the full digits+fraction (or digits+unit) shape as one token — splitting one logical value into two # tokens instead of one. This makes the normalized SHAPE depend on whether the integer part crosses the hex rule's 7-digit threshold, so two otherwise-identical incidental-noise messages straddling that boundary fail to collapse into the same digest. Verified empirically against the freshly rebuilt dist (packages/main/dist/core/convergence-breaker.js) at HEAD 68f2fabbe9 (round-3 commit ba2ac008e5): gateFailureDigest("story_advance","heartbeat 123456.5ms ago") !== gateFailureDigest("story_advance","heartbeat 1234567.5ms ago") (DISTINCT — both are pure wall-clock noise per the duration rule's own stated purpose and should collapse), while gateFailureDigest of two 7+-digit fractional durations against EACH OTHER, and two <7-digit fractional durations against EACH OTHER, both correctly COLLAPSE — isolating the defect to exactly the digit-count-crossing case. Same effect on the plain number rule: "attempt 41.5 failed" vs "attempt 1234567.5 failed" is DISTINCT. This is the identical failure class F-007/F-015 were filed to fix (a genuine retry sequence silently mints a fresh key and the repeat counter never reaches 2, so assessBreaker never trips gate-repeat for that pair) but for the newly-introduced hex/duration-number lookaround asymmetry, and none of the 24 CHK-004 matrix cases exercise a free-standing decimal with a >=7-digit integer part (the only hex-adjacent must-differ case, identifier-attached-long-decimal, is hyphen-attached with no fractional dot). Fix: give the hex rule the same (?<!\d\.)/(?!\.\d) lookarounds as the duration/number rules, or otherwise ensure it does not consume a digit run immediately followed by .digit.
findings.resolvedReason: The free-standing hash rule now carries the dot-adjacency lookarounds it was missing: (?<![\w-])(?<!\d\.)[0-9a-f]{7,}(?![\w-])(?!\.\d). findings.desc: CHK-004:edge:0 and CHK-004:adversarial:0 verificationEvidence (checklist.json) claim the 24-case matrix and its nine revert-proofs comprehensively guard the must-still-collapse direction ('proving the breaker keeps catching a genuine repeat'; 'each leaving all other cases passing'), but this is not true against the exact code at the current HEAD: B-bf52:F-016 (open, unresolved, filed by lattice-review-quality at RR-014 against the same head 68f2fabbe9/material 141ee128..., code unchanged since) shows the hex rule (convergence-breaker.ts:556) lacks the (?<!\d\.)/(?!\.\d) dot-adjacency lookarounds that the duration rule (:588) and number rule (:612) both carry, so a free-standing decimal or duration whose integer part is >=7 digits gets split across the hex and duration/number rules and fails to collapse. findings.desc: cross-host (codex-cli host-B round 3), recorded by the main agent: matrix case identifier-attached-long-decimal is tagged solely hex-rule-overreach but also depends on the number rule staying narrow. findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/convergence-breaker.ts gateFailureDigest still silently disarms the breaker for a THIRD real story_advance-reachable producer: the ownership-gate rejection embeds the BLOCKED (current) session id via formatNonOwnerError (core/story-owner-lease.ts:636-638 "so this session (${ctx.currentSessionId}) cannot run it"), fed by cli/ownership-gate.ts:317 currentSessionId: getSessionId(). Whenever LATTICE_SESSION_ID and every supported host-adapter env var (CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID, CODEX_*, ANTIGRAVITY_*, ...) are absent, owner-session.ts:28-32 deriveLocalSessionId falls back to sessionSource=derived-ppid and mints sess-${sha256(host,root,ppid).slice(0,16)} -- a value that changes on EVERY fresh CLI invocation because process.ppid differs per process (this is the code's own documented degraded path: owner-session.ts:83 warns "session identity degraded: derived-ppid; export LATTICE_SESSION_ID ... before repeated mutating commands"). Verified empirically: two separate node invocations in this worktree with no session env vars set produced ppid 8629 -> sess-d7efe197b316c43a and ppid 16456 -> sess-f278b84bbcb06149. Because this 16-hex-char suffix is attached to "sess" by a HYPHEN, convergence-breaker.ts's hex rule (:556), duration rule (:588) and number rule (:612) all treat it as a protected identifier (their shared (?<![\w-]) lookbehind excludes hyphen-attached runs) and never normalize it -- correct for a STABLE identifier like a story id, wrong here because this specific suffix is per-process noise, not identity. Reproduced end-to-end against the built dist with the real functions (deriveLocalSessionId + formatNonOwnerError + gateFailureDigest): two renderings of the identical real ownership-gate rejection (same foreign owner B-bf52 lease, same command, differing only in the blocked session's derived-ppid suffix) hash to story_advance/6bad05ab768c vs story_advance/48de9a1498fe -- they do NOT collapse. Consequence: an agent or human retrying story_advance against a live foreign lease with no session-id env configured (plain terminal, CI script, or any unsupported host harness -- the exact same class of caller the derived-ppid warning already flags) mints a brand-new gate-failure-counts.json key on every single retry; maxGateFailureCount never reaches 2 and the convergence breaker never trips for this genuinely repeating rejection -- the same silent-non-firing failure mode as F-007/F-014, via a different real producer this round's fix did not cover. Fix direction: normalize the derived-ppid sess-<hex> suffix specifically (e.g. treat a hyphen-attached hex run of 12+ chars immediately following the literal token "sess-" as volatile), or have formatNonOwnerError omit/shorten the untrusted local session id from the message text used for counting, without touching the CHK-002/CHK-003 identifier-preservation guarantees for real identifiers like story ids and checklist ids.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed with a new attached-hash rule at position 2 of the chain: (?<=[-_])(?=[0-9a-f]*[a-f])[0-9a-f]{7,}(?![\w-]) -> #. A hyphen or underscore attached run of 7+ hex characters CONTAINING AT LEAST ONE a-f LETTER is provably a digest and never a human ordinal, so sess-d7efe197b316c43a collapses while session-1234567 and worker-1721775600 stay distinct — the letter requirement is what satisfies this finding without reopening F-014, and it is the one place where a SHAPE cleanly separates the two directions a bare number cannot. Chosen over the findings alternative of special-casing the literal sess- token because it is structural rather than an enumeration. Guarded by must-still-collapse case ppid-derived-session-id, which CALLS the real deriveLocalSessionId and the real formatNonOwnerError rendering rather than imitating them, varies only the PPID, and asserts both generated digests actually contain an a-f letter so the fixture cannot silently degenerate into one that passes for the wrong reason. Revert-proved: deleting the rule fails that case and no other.

findings.desc: cross-host (codex-cli host-B round 4), recorded by the main agent: the ppid-derived-session-id fixture varies the LEASE OWNER session id while claiming to model one retrying host. formatNonOwnerError (story-owner-lease.ts:636) renders lease.sessionId as the owner and ctx.currentSessionId as the rejected caller; a genuine retry against the same owner keeps lease.sessionId CONSTANT, and a change to it means ownership actually changed, i.e. a substantively different failure. Same token shape, opposite requirement by position: the attached-hash rule cannot distinguish them.

cross-host (codex-cli host-B round 4), recorded by the main agent: the attached-hash rule requires an a-f letter to prove a run is a digest, which leaves an unbounded retry hole for all-decimal digest prefixes. codex brute-forced deriveLocalSessionId over ppid values and found real examples sess-0378592327422727 and sess-1686256634242425 whose rejection renderings produce DISTINCT keys. findings.desc: cross-host (codex-cli host-B round 6), recorded by the main agent: sep- is a REAL substantive artifact-id prefix wrongly placed in the completeness guard exclusion list at convergence-breaker-smoke.ts:871. Producer scope-anti-expansion.ts:120 mints SEP-<storyId>-<NNN>; machine.ts:269 renders them into a story_advance INIT_CHECK rejection. SEP-B-bf52-001 and SEP-B-bf52-002 collapse to story_advance/e2db55c93f47, so a host resolving scope-extension proposals sequentially falsely freezes. This is an F-029-class hole hidden inside the guard: the scan DOES discover sep-, but the false exclusion makes it report all-classified. TWO fixes required: (1) remove sep- from the exclusion list and make it substantive; (2) SEP is a COMPOUND id SEP-<storyId>-<ordinal> where only the final ordinal is substantive and the storyId in the middle is constant within a per-story counter, so the allowlist mechanism (which only inspects the single prefix immediately before a digit run) cannot protect the trailing ordinal by adding sep- alone; the digit rule must recognise a substantive artifact id as a WHOLE token (an allowlisted prefix followed by the rest of its id ending in a digit) and protect it entire. Main agent validated a whole-token approach 17/17 including SEP-001 vs SEP-002 distinct while b-1234/b-5678, story ids, attempts, heartbeats and RR- all still collapse.
findings.resolvedReason: sep- removed from the exclusion list and added to SUBSTANTIVE_ID_PREFIXES, and the underlying mechanism replaced: a substantive artifact id is now matched as a WHOLE TOKEN (allowlisted prefix, then the rest of the id, ending in a digit) and lifted out before normalization, so the compound SEP-B-bf52-001 is protected entire rather than only up to the prefix immediately before a digit run. The digit rule reverts to main's bare /\d+/g since the allowlist is applied by the extraction step. The placeholder index is encoded in a non-digit non-hex alphabet between U+0001 sentinels; a numeric index would be rewritten by the bare-number rule and every kept token would restore identically (mutation M13 reproduces exactly that trap and is caught by 5 matrix cases). Verified: matrix case scope-extension-proposal-ordinal (guard substantive-id-whole-token) is the ONLY case that fails when whole-token matching is reverted to prefix-before-digits with the allowlist left intact; SEP-...-001 vs -002 digest distinctly while b-1234/b-5678, heartbeats, bare attempts, RR- and RL- all still collapse. gate-repeat-block-smoke.ts stays byte-unmodified and exits 0.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/convergence-breaker.ts:673 — the signals-conditional 200-char prefix cut is NOT relaxed when two rejections have an IDENTICAL, non-empty signal set but differ only in an embedded allowlisted ordinal past char 200. extractGateBlockSignals only captures the gap CODE (e.g. milestone_source_requirement_unbound, acceptance_binding_unknown_checklist_ref), never the specific object the gap names, so two genuinely different ProofStory DEV-gate rejections collapse. Repro with 100% real production code (core/proofstory.ts renderProofStoryDiagnosticReport + the exact machine.ts:179 banner + bumpGateFailureCount): a milestone-ledger gap naming sourceRequirementId REQ-001 vs the SAME gap code naming REQ-002 on a different milestone digest IDENTICALLY (story_advance/b5117552c0ff both times) even though REQ- is allowlisted and the strings genuinely diverge at char 450 (past the 200-char cut). Same mechanism reproduced with acceptance_binding_unknown_checklist_ref naming CHK-005 vs CHK-006 (also identical digest, story_advance/011867525d4e both times) — so this is a GENERAL flaw affecting any/all of the 7 allowlisted prefixes when they appear inside a ProofStory diagnostic-gap message, not one specific prefix. Confirmed end-to-end: two bumpGateFailureCount calls with these real REQ-001/REQ-002 renders leave maxGateFailureCount=2, the exact breaker-trip threshold — a false freeze on a story making incremental progress (fix REQ-001, then get correctly blocked by the separate, later-discovered REQ-002 gap), which is precisely the class of bug CHK-001 exists to close. tasks/convergence-breaker-smoke.ts signals-fold/proofstory-gap-signal-set case only tests DIFFERENT gap codes (assert.notDeepEqual(sigA, sigB) at line ~412) and never tests the SAME gap code recurring with a different embedded ordinal, so this gap is untested. Fix direction: extractGateBlockSignals must also capture the substantive ordinal(s) embedded inside each gap message (not just the code), or the signals-branch prefix must not be capped at 200 when the message contains an allowlisted-prefix ordinal beyond that cut.
findings.resolvedReason: Accepted as a documented residual rather than fixed, and the acceptance is measured rather than argued. When two rejections extract an IDENTICAL signal set and differ only in a substantive ordinal past character 200 of the normalized reason, they still share one key. This is NEVER WORSE THAN MAIN: main truncates at 200 unconditionally AND rewrites every ordinal to #, so main collapses that same pair and also collapses the within-window pair this branch keeps apart. The improvement is therefore bounded, not regressive.
